summary: The LSP subsystem gives the loop semantic code intelligence by speaking Language Server Protocol (JSON-RPC 2.0 / Content-Length over stdio) to external language servers. As a client (LspClient) it lazily launches rust-analyzer, pyright, typescript-language-server, or gopls based on file extension, opens documents, and answers goto_definition, find_references, document_symbols, hover, workspace_symbol, goto_implementation, and diagnostics. As a server (SelfwareLspServer / run_lsp_server) selfware itself answers documentSymbol, workspace/symbol, definition, and hover from its ProjectIntelligence symbol index so editors like Zed can query it. On the loop it is primarily a 'perceive' node — it turns positions and queries into grounded Symbols, Locations, Hovers, and Diagnostics — while diagnostics feed the 'verify' stage.
context_basis: Recommendations were formed by reading src/lsp/ (client.rs, server.rs, mod.rs) in the context of the full engine's ~600k-token budget framing, so each move accounts for how a precise LSP fact replaces reading whole files and thereby conserves the loop's token budget.

examples.title: Lazily launch the right server by file extension
examples.intent: Bring semantic intelligence online for a file only when the loop first touches it.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: LspClient defers spawning until a query arrives, then Language::from_path picks the language and server_candidates the binary; the first working candidate becomes the connection, so the loop pays server-start cost only for languages it actually inspects.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Drag a source file onto the LSP node to bind it; the node auto-selects and launches the matching language server.
touch_interaction.visual: A language glyph (Rust/Py/TS/Go) fades in and the node ring spins during spawn, then settles solid.

examples.mini_scenario: The loop queries src/main.rs; from_path returns Rust, rust-analyzer is found on PATH, and the connection comes up on demand.
examples.pitfall: If no candidate binary exists, the client errors — don't wire an LSP query as a hard dependency without a fallback to plain file reads.

examples.title: Open a document before querying it
examples.intent: Give the server the file content so its answers reflect the loop's working state.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: did_open sends textDocument/didOpen with the current content; the server indexes it so subsequent goto/hover/diagnostics operate on what the loop sees, not stale disk state.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tap the file chip on the LSP node to push its buffer to the server (didOpen).
touch_interaction.visual: The chip flashes then wears a small open-book badge indicating the document is synced.

examples.mini_scenario: Before asking for symbols, did_open streams the edited buffer so document_symbols reflects the uncommitted change.
examples.pitfall: Query without did_open and the server may answer from stale or absent content — always sync the buffer first.

examples.title: Jump to a definition to ground a plan
examples.intent: Resolve where a symbol is defined so the loop edits the right place.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: goto_definition returns Vec<Location> {file,line,column}; the planner uses the precise site instead of grepping, so the next act step targets exact coordinates.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Double-tap a symbol token on the code preview to jump the canvas to its definition node.
touch_interaction.visual: A comet edge arcs from the call site to the definition node, which pulses on arrival.

examples.mini_scenario: The plan needs to change fn parse(); goto_definition returns parser.rs:88:4 and the edit step targets it directly.
examples.pitfall: Multiple Locations can come back for overloaded or ambiguous symbols — don't assume the first is authoritative without checking the file.

examples.title: Find references before a risky rename
examples.intent: Enumerate every use of a symbol so a rename or signature change is complete.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: find_references returns all Locations touching the symbol; the loop expands its edit plan to cover each site, turning a single edit into a bounded multi-site act.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Spread over a symbol node to fan out every reference as a constellation of call-site nodes.
touch_interaction.visual: Reference nodes bloom outward, each labeled file:line, connected by faint edges to the origin.

examples.mini_scenario: Renaming Config::load, find_references surfaces 12 call sites; the plan edits all 12 in one pass.
examples.pitfall: References are a snapshot — if the loop edits files between the scan and the act, re-query, or a stale Location misses a moved use.

examples.title: Outline a file with document symbols
examples.intent: Get a file's shape without reading its full text into the budget.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: document_symbols returns Vec<SymbolInfo> {name,kind,line,column}; the loop perceives the file's functions/structs/methods cheaply and plans against the outline rather than the raw source.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Pinch a file node to collapse its full text into a compact symbol outline strip.
touch_interaction.visual: Lines of code fold into labeled kind-colored rows (fn/struct/method), preserving order and indentation.

examples.mini_scenario: Instead of reading 900 lines, the loop pulls document_symbols and sees the 14 functions it needs to reason about.
examples.pitfall: SymbolInfo.kind is a human-readable string, not an enum — match on the exact strings the server emits, not assumed variants.

examples.title: Hover for a signature instead of reading source
examples.intent: Learn a symbol's type/signature with a single cheap probe.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: hover returns Option<String> markdown; the loop resolves a signature or type in one small evidence packet rather than opening the defining file, conserving token budget.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-press a symbol token to float its hover card with type and doc inline.
touch_interaction.visual: A markdown tooltip lifts above the token with a soft glow; empty hovers show a muted 'no info' state.

examples.mini_scenario: The loop hovers `db.query` and gets the full generic signature, so it calls it correctly without reading the crate.
examples.pitfall: hover returns None legitimately when the server has nothing — treat None as 'unknown', not as an error to recover from.

examples.title: Collect diagnostics as a verify gate
examples.intent: Check whether an edit introduced errors before the loop advances.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: diagnostics returns the cached Vec<Diagnostic> from the last textDocument/publishDiagnostics; an error-severity entry fails the verify gate and can route the loop to ErrorRecovery.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tap the diagnostics badge on a file node to list current errors and warnings.
touch_interaction.visual: The node ring turns red on any error-severity diagnostic, amber on warnings, green when clean.

examples.mini_scenario: After an edit, diagnostics shows an error at line 40; the verify gate blocks the commit and the loop fixes it.
examples.pitfall: Diagnostics are cached from the last publish — after an edit, give the server a moment to re-publish or you'll gate on stale results.

examples.title: Search the workspace for a symbol
examples.intent: Find a symbol by name across the whole project without knowing its file.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: workspace_symbol(query) returns matching Vec<SymbolInfo> project-wide; the loop locates an entity from a name alone, seeding a plan without a prior file target.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Draw from a search bubble to the LSP node to run a workspace symbol query.
touch_interaction.visual: Matching symbol nodes light up across the canvas map, ranked by relevance with count badge.

examples.mini_scenario: The loop searches 'Budget' and workspace_symbol returns the struct plus its methods across three files.
examples.pitfall: Broad queries can return many matches — narrow the query or the planner wastes budget triaging noise.

examples.title: Go to implementation from a trait
examples.intent: Resolve which concrete type implements an interface at a call site.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: goto_implementation returns implementation Locations; the loop bridges from a trait/interface to real code, so it can reason about actual behavior rather than the abstract signature.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Double-tap a trait node to fan out to its implementor nodes.
touch_interaction.visual: Dashed abstraction edges resolve into solid edges pointing at each concrete impl node.

examples.mini_scenario: The plan hits Tool::execute; goto_implementation lists McpTool and the native tools that implement it.
examples.pitfall: Not all servers implement goto_implementation richly — handle an empty result as 'server can't answer', not 'no implementors'.

examples.title: Map diagnostic severity to loop response
examples.intent: Let error vs warning vs hint drive different loop branches.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: Diagnostic.severity is 'error'|'warning'|'info'|'hint' (mapped from numeric 1–4); the verify step blocks on error, notes warnings, and lets hints inform learn without halting.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-press the diagnostics badge to break the count down by severity tier.
touch_interaction.visual: A stacked bar shows red/amber/blue/grey segments for error/warning/info/hint counts.

examples.mini_scenario: An edit yields one warning and two hints but no error; the loop commits and records the hints for later cleanup.
examples.pitfall: Don't halt on warnings by default — over-strict gating on non-error severities stalls otherwise-valid progress.

examples.title: Close documents to bound server state
examples.intent: Release documents the loop is done with so server memory stays bounded.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: did_close sends textDocument/didClose; over a long loop this keeps the language server's open-document set from growing without limit as files are visited and abandoned.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Flick a synced file chip off the LSP node to close its document.
touch_interaction.visual: The open-book badge closes and the chip dims to indicate the server released it.

examples.mini_scenario: After editing and verifying config.rs, the loop closes it so the server isn't holding dozens of stale buffers.
examples.pitfall: Close only what you're finished with — closing a file mid-plan drops its diagnostics and forces a re-open.

examples.title: Shut down all servers on loop teardown
examples.intent: Reclaim every language-server process when the loop ends.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: shutdown sends the shutdown request then exit notification and kills each process; the loop returns the process budget it borrowed across all launched languages.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Flick the LSP node to the canvas edge to tear down all its connections at once.
touch_interaction.visual: Each language sub-node shrinks and fades in sequence; a final exit glyph confirms full teardown.

examples.mini_scenario: The task finishes having used rust-analyzer and gopls; shutdown reaps both processes cleanly.
examples.pitfall: Skipping shutdown leaks a long-lived language server per language — always tear down even on the error path.

examples.title: Serve selfware's own symbol index over LSP
examples.intent: Let an editor query selfware's ProjectIntelligence as if it were a language server.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: run_lsp_server starts SelfwareLspServer answering documentSymbol, workspace/symbol, definition, and hover from ProjectIntelligence; the loop's perception layer becomes an external editor's, inverting client and host.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Flick the symbol-index node outward past the canvas edge to publish it as an LSP surface.
touch_interaction.visual: The node gains a broadcast halo and an inbound-arrow glyph as editor requests begin flowing in.

examples.mini_scenario: Zed connects to selfware's LSP server and workspace/symbol returns the CodeGraph symbols from ProjectIntelligence.
examples.pitfall: ProjectIntelligence is refreshed per request (no cache) — that keeps results fresh but adds latency, so don't fan out one request per keystroke.

examples.title: Resolve a token at a cursor position
examples.intent: Turn a raw (line,column) into the identifier the user means.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: SelfwareLspServer walks identifier characters (alphanumeric + underscore) around the position, with a fallback to the previous char, so definition/hover resolve even when the cursor sits at a token boundary.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tap precisely on a token in the code preview to resolve the identifier under the point.
touch_interaction.visual: The resolved identifier highlights with a selection box; a boundary-fallback shows a small left-arrow hint.

examples.mini_scenario: The cursor lands just past `parse`; the fallback checks the previous char, resolves `parse`, and hover returns its signature.
examples.pitfall: Positions are 1-indexed line/column in this server — off-by-one indexing silently resolves the wrong token.

examples.title: Format hover as signature plus location
examples.intent: Return just enough context — the signature and where it lives — as one markdown packet.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: SelfwareLspServer builds hover markdown as `signature\nfile:line` from the matched Symbol; the loop gets a self-contained Evidence card it can quote without a follow-up read.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-press a symbol node to surface its formatted hover card.
touch_interaction.visual: A markdown card shows the signature on top and a dimmed file:line footer beneath.

examples.mini_scenario: Hovering a struct returns `pub struct Budget { ... }` plus `resource/budget.rs:22`, enough to reason without opening the file.
examples.pitfall: Keep the hover compact — dumping the whole symbol body defeats the budget savings the hover exists to provide.

examples.title: Auto-detect Content-Length framing on the wire
examples.intent: Read LSP-framed messages regardless of how the peer chunks its writes.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: Both LSP client and server frame with Content-Length headers via the shared mcp::transport read/write helpers; the loop's perceive channel stays intact even when a header and body arrive in separate reads.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Pinch the transport node to inspect the header/body framing of the last message.
touch_interaction.visual: A framed envelope glyph shows the Content-Length header split from its JSON body.

examples.mini_scenario: rust-analyzer sends a header line then the body in a second write; read_message assembles both into one JSON-RPC message.
examples.pitfall: LSP uses Content-Length framing, not newline-delimited — mixing MCP's default newline framing here truncates messages.

examples.title: Sanitize the server environment for toolchain vars only
examples.intent: Launch a language server with just the toolchain discovery vars it needs and no secrets.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: The client clears secrets (SELFWARE_API_KEY, AWS_*, GITHUB_TOKEN) and whitelists only CARGO_HOME, RUSTUP_HOME, NODE_PATH, PYTHONPATH, VIRTUAL_ENV, GOPATH, GOROOT, JAVA_HOME, so the loop can perceive safely via third-party servers.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-press the language sub-node to inspect the sanitized env passed to its server.
touch_interaction.visual: Secret vars render struck-through in red; whitelisted toolchain vars glow green as passed through.

examples.mini_scenario: gopls launches seeing GOPATH and GOROOT but not the operator's GITHUB_TOKEN, so it can resolve modules without touching credentials.
examples.pitfall: A server that needs an unlisted var to find its toolchain will fail quietly — extend the whitelist deliberately, never disable the firewall.

examples.title: Time out a stalled server query
examples.intent: Keep a hung language server from freezing the loop's perceive step.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: Each request awaits its oneshot with a 30s timeout; on expiry the client returns an explicit error so the loop can fall back to a file read rather than blocking indefinitely.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tap an in-flight query edge to see its remaining timeout countdown.
touch_interaction.visual: A thinning ring counts down around the edge; at zero it snaps red with a timeout badge.

examples.mini_scenario: rust-analyzer is still indexing and a goto_definition hangs; at 30s the client errors and the loop reads the file directly.
examples.pitfall: A cold server can exceed 30s during initial indexing — don't treat the first timeout as a fatal server failure, retry once.

examples.title: Suppress responses for notifications
examples.intent: Reply only to requests, never to fire-and-forget notifications.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: SelfwareLspServer sends a JsonRpcResponse only when the incoming request carries an id; didOpen/didChange/didClose and initialized are accepted silently, keeping the loop's message flow correct.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Flick a notification pulse at the server node; it absorbs without emitting a reply edge.
touch_interaction.visual: Notification pulses fade into the node with no return animation; id-bearing requests spawn a reply edge.

examples.mini_scenario: The editor streams didChange notifications as the user types; the server updates state and answers none of them.
examples.pitfall: Emitting a response to a notification confuses the client's correlation table — check for id before ever writing a reply.

examples.title: Convert file URIs safely across the boundary
examples.intent: Translate between file:// URIs and filesystem paths without corrupting either.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: uri_to_path and path_to_uri use url::Url so definitions and symbols cross the LSP boundary as valid file:// URIs; the loop's Locations resolve to real paths the act step can open.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Double-tap a Location node to expand its file:// URI and resolved path side by side.
touch_interaction.visual: The URI and path render as paired chips; a mismatch highlights amber if conversion fails.

examples.mini_scenario: A definition response carries file:///Users/ivo/selfware/src/main.rs; uri_to_path resolves it and the edit step opens the file.
examples.pitfall: Hand-splicing file:// strings breaks on spaces and special characters — always round-trip through url::Url, never string concatenation.
